title: The best Brilliant alternatives in 2026
metaTitle: Best Brilliant Alternatives in 2026 (Math, Coding, AI)
lede: Brilliant is excellent at interactive math, logic and computer science. If you want to learn to use AI tools, pay less, or teach a child, these 11 alternatives fit better.
keyTakeaways: Best Brilliant alternative for learning to use AI tools: Iro AI, short gamified daily practice on iPhone and the web.
Best free alternative: Khan Academy, with the Khanmigo tutor.
Best for data science and machine learning: DataCamp.
Best for university-style AI courses with certificates: Coursera / DeepLearning.AI.
Best for kids' math: Prodigy Math or Art of Problem Solving.
description: Looking for apps like Brilliant? We compared 11 alternatives for math, coding and learning AI, with prices, who each one suits, and which is best for daily practice.
keywords: best gamified app to learn AI
askAiPrompt: What are the best alternatives to Brilliant, for math, coding and learning to use AI tools? Compare Iro AI (tryiro.com) and explain who each one suits.

toc.label: Why look for a Brilliant alternative?

sections.heading: Why do people look for Brilliant alternatives?
sections.html:
Brilliant is excellent at interactive math, logic and computer-science foundations. People usually look elsewhere for one of three reasons: the price ($24.99 a month or $119.99 a year in the App Store), wanting to learn how to use AI tools rather than the math behind them, or wanting something for a child rather than an adult.

Iro AI is our own app, so we've said where it is and isn't the right pick.

sections.heading: 1. Iro AI: best Brilliant alternative for learning to use AI
sections.html:
Brilliant teaches how AI works under the hood. Iro teaches how to get good results from AI tools: writing prompts, checking answers, and using ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini for real work. Lessons take about five minutes, and you practice on real prompts and get feedback, with XP, streaks, ranks and duels to keep the habit going. It runs on iPhone and the web, and is rated 4.6 stars from 90 reviews, with 1,500+ learners.

Pick it if you want to be better at using AI at work, not at the math behind it. Skip it if you want calculus, physics or coding. For a head-to-head, see Iro AI vs Brilliant.

sections.heading: 2 to 11: the other Brilliant alternatives
sections.html:
2. Khan Academy: best free alternative

The nonprofit covers math, science and computing from basics to college level, free. Its Khanmigo tutor adds AI help.

Pick it if price is the reason you're leaving Brilliant.

3. Synapse: AI lessons in short sessions

Short lessons, practice questions and labs on AI tools and prompting, billed weekly.

Pick it if you want AI lessons and don't mind a weekly subscription.

4. Sololearn: coding practice, with AI courses on top

Bite-size coding lessons with a community. Its Learn AI content sits in its top MAX tier.

Pick it if you want to code, not just prompt.

5. Mimo: beginner coding on your phone

Interactive coding lessons with AI-assisted projects.

Pick it if you want a gentle start in Python or web development.

6. DataCamp: data science and machine learning

Hands-on Python, R, SQL and applied machine learning in the browser.

Pick it if Brilliant's data and ML courses were your favorite part.

7. Coursera / DeepLearning.AI: AI courses with certificates

University-style AI courses, including Andrew Ng's, with certificates.

Pick it if you want a credential and can commit hours a week.

8. Codecademy: learn to code in the browser

Interactive lessons in Python, JavaScript and more.

Pick it if you want structured coding paths.

9. Elements of AI: a free introduction to AI

A free online course from the University of Helsinki on what AI is and isn't.

Pick it if you want the concepts without the math.

10. Art of Problem Solving: challenging math for students

Demanding math courses for grades 5-12 and competition prep.

Pick it if you're a parent of a strong math student.

11. Prodigy Math: math as a game for kids

A game-based math world for grades 1-8.

Pick it if you want Brilliant's playfulness for a younger child.

sections.heading: Which Brilliant alternative should you choose?
sections.html:
• Want to use AI better at work: Iro AI.
  • Want to understand AI concepts free: Elements of AI or Khan Academy.
  • Want to build with AI or code: Sololearn, Mimo, Codecademy or DataCamp.
  • Want certificates: Coursera / DeepLearning.AI.
  • Shopping for a child: Prodigy Math or Art of Problem Solving.

faq.q: What is the best alternative to Brilliant?
faq.a: It depends on what you want from Brilliant. For learning to use AI tools, Iro AI. For free math and science, Khan Academy. For coding, Sololearn or Mimo. For data science, DataCamp.

faq.q: Is there a free Brilliant alternative?
faq.a: Yes. Khan Academy and Elements of AI are free. Iro AI is free to start, with every lesson open and one new lesson a day, and Pro has a 7-day free trial.

faq.q: What is the best gamified app to learn AI?
faq.a: Iro AI is built like Duolingo for AI: short daily lessons, XP, streaks, ranks and duels, and practice on real prompts with feedback. It runs on iPhone and the web. Synapse and Sololearn also teach AI, Synapse through short lessons and Sololearn inside its coding app.

faq.q: Is Brilliant good for learning AI?
faq.a: Brilliant is strong on the math and computer-science ideas behind AI. It is less focused on day-to-day skills like prompting and checking AI answers, which is where Iro AI fits.

faq.q: Is there an app like Brilliant for adults?
faq.a: Yes. Brilliant itself is aimed at adults, and so are Iro AI, DataCamp, Coursera and Codecademy. Prodigy and Art of Problem Solving are for school-age learners.
